key_insight: LEXIS introduces InterFields — dense, continuous proximity signatures (LatEnt ProXimal Interaction Signatures) — that encode fine-grained body–object spatial coupling from a single RGB image, enabling more physically plausible 3D human–object interaction reconstructions than sparse binary contact cues.
problem_solved: How to recover realistic 3D human–object interactions from a single RGB image by modeling subtle, continuous proximity and dense spatial relationships between body and objects, which binary contact signals cannot capture.
method: Represent interactions as dense continuous proximity fields (InterFields) — latent signatures that describe per-location proximity between human and object geometry.
Learn an encoder that maps a single RGB image into latent proximal signatures and decoders that reconstruct 3D human pose/shape, object geometry, and proximity fields.
Use the dense proximity fields to guide geometry refinement and physically-plausible contact reasoning (replacing sparse binary contact cues with continuous spatial coupling).
impact: Provides practitioners a compact, learnable representation for richer interaction reasoning from images, improving 3D HOI reconstruction quality and enabling more reliable downstream applications (robot manipulation, AR/VR, scene understanding) that require physically plausible human–object coupling.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: RGB image → encoder → latent InterFields → decoders producing 3D human, 3D object, and proximity field overlays.
Side-by-side comparison: binary contact map vs. dense InterField heatmap showing smoother, spatially-detailed proximity.
3D render overlays: reconstructed human+object with proximity field shown as colored distance contours indicating degrees of coupling.
Use-case icons: robotics manipulation, AR object interaction, and scene understanding with short captions about benefits.
paper_title: LEXIS: LatEnt ProXimal Interaction Signatures for 3D HOI from an Image
paper_authors: Dimitrije Antić, Alvaro Budria, George Paschalidis, Sai Kumar Dwivedi, Dimitrios Tzionas
